k8s-004.definition: Role-based access control. A Role lists allowed verbs, API groups and resources inside a namespace, and a RoleBinding grants that Role to a subject.
A scope that partitions most API object names and namespaced permissions within one cluster, so the same name can exist separately in two namespaces.
The authenticated user or ServiceAccount that sends a request. Authorization is decided for that identity, not for whoever typed the command.
The course's private reservation of one disposable cluster and namespace, which defines the only target a lab command may change.
A named kubeconfig entry that combines a cluster, a user and a default namespace. Selecting it explicitly keeps a command from reaching whatever target was last active.

k8s-005.definition: The smallest Kubernetes scheduling and lifecycle unit, holding one or more containers that share a network identity and can share volumes.
The container field that tells the kubelet when to pull an image. With Never, the kubelet uses only a locally present image and reports an error instead of fetching one.
A broad lifecycle summary such as Pending, Running or Succeeded. Running does not mean every container is ready to serve.
The per-container status of Waiting, Running or Terminated, with a reason such as ErrImageNeverPull or an exit code.
The output captured from one container process. A container that never started has no application log to read.

k8s-006.definition: A workload controller that manages ReplicaSets to keep a declared number of identical Pods running and to roll out template changes.
The controller object that keeps a stable count of Pods matching its selector. A Deployment creates a new ReplicaSet for each Pod template revision.
The specification stored in the API, such as replicas and the Pod template, that controllers work to make true.
The repeated controller process of comparing desired state with observed state and acting to close the difference.
A metadata link from a dependent object, such as a Pod, to the controller object that created and manages it.

k8s-007.definition: A key and value pair in object metadata, such as app=hello, used to group and select objects.
A query over labels that a Service or controller uses to choose its member Pods. A selector that matches nothing leaves a Service without endpoints.
A stable name and virtual address that routes traffic to the ready Pods its selector matches.
The default Service type, which gives the Service a virtual IP address reachable from inside the cluster.
The Service field naming the container port, by number or name, that receives traffic sent to the Service port.

k8s-009.definition: An API object that stores non-secret configuration as key and value data for Pods to consume.
A container env entry that reads one ConfigMap key. Its value is resolved when the container starts and does not change inside a running process.
A volume that projects ConfigMap keys as files. The kubelet refreshes mounted files after an unspecified delay, and subPath mounts behave differently.
The application's own step of rereading changed configuration. Without it, a new value needs a new container process to take effect.

k8s-010.definition: The CPU and memory amount the scheduler reserves for a container when choosing a node.
The maximum CPU or memory a container may use. Exceeding a memory limit can end the container with OOMKilled, while CPU above the limit is throttled.
A namespace object that caps total requests, limits or object counts, so admission rejects a create that would exceed it.
One thousandth of a CPU, written with the m suffix, so 100m means 0.1 CPU.
A Pod accepted by the API but not yet running, often because no node has enough unreserved resources for its requests.

k8s-011.definition: A workload controller that runs Pods until a specified number of them complete successfully.
A controller that creates Jobs on a cron schedule. Its suspend field pauses future runs without deleting existing Jobs.
The Job field that sets how many Pod failures are retried before the Job is marked failed.
The Job field that bounds total run time. When the deadline passes, the Job stops its Pods and records a failure.
The integer a container process returns when it ends. In this lesson 0 means success and 2 is the allowed failure outcome.

k8s-012.definition: A recorded field value, event or bounded log line from a named owned object. It is evidence, unlike a guess about cause.
A candidate explanation for a symptom that a specific observation could support or rule out.
A typed status entry such as Ready or Available, with a status, reason and message that report one aspect of an object.
A short-lived API record of something a component did or saw, such as a scheduling decision or a failed image pull.
An ordered record from source submission through API acceptance, scheduling, container start, readiness and client behavior that shows where a failure began.

k8s-013.definition: The controlled replacement of Pods from an old template revision with Pods from a new one.
A numbered version of a Deployment's Pod template, carried by the ReplicaSet that runs it.
A counter the API server increments when an object's desired spec changes. Comparing it with status.observedGeneration shows whether the controller has processed the change.
Returning a Deployment to an earlier Pod template, which itself proceeds as a new rollout.
A period when Pods from old and new revisions are ready at the same time, so clients can reach either version.

k8s-014.definition: A service whose replicas keep no data that must survive a Pod replacement, so any ready replica can answer any request.
A Job that sends a fixed number of requests to the Service with timeouts and exits with a result, giving an application-level check.
A result that looks healthy, such as Running Pods and an existing Service, while the application path fails.
The ready Pod addresses a Service currently routes to. An empty set means the Service exists but no backend receives traffic.
Deleting only the objects whose API-assigned UIDs were recorded at creation, so cleanup cannot remove an object the lesson does not own.

k8s-015.definition: A check that holds off liveness and readiness probes until a slow-starting application first succeeds.
A check that decides whether a container should receive Service traffic. Failing it removes the Pod from ready endpoints without restarting it.
A check whose repeated failure makes the kubelet restart the container. A probe that is too strict causes needless restarts.
The number of consecutive probe failures required before the kubelet acts on that probe.
The per-container counter that rises each time the kubelet restarts that container inside the same Pod.

k8s-016.definition: A container that runs to completion before the application containers start. Each init container must succeed before the next one begins.
A volume created empty for a Pod and shared by its containers. It survives container restarts and is removed with the Pod.
The kubelet starting a new process for a container in the same Pod, which keeps the Pod UID and its emptyDir data.
A controller creating a new Pod with a new UID, which starts with a fresh emptyDir.
A file holding the Pod UID that shows whether data survived a container restart or belongs to a replaced Pod.

k8s-017.definition: Pod and container settings that request the process user, privilege escalation, capabilities and filesystem restrictions.
A built-in admission check that enforces the Privileged, Baseline or Restricted Pod Security Standard chosen for a namespace.
A securityContext field that makes the kubelet refuse to start a container whose process would run as user 0.
A securityContext field that, when false, stops a process from gaining more privileges than its parent, for example through setuid.
Linux capabilities removed from a container process, each taking away one specific privileged kernel operation.

k8s-018.definition: A namespaced identity for processes in Pods. RBAC bindings grant it permissions just as they do for users.
An object that grants a Role's rules to subjects, such as a ServiceAccount, within one namespace.
The API that issues a bounded ServiceAccount token for a specified audience and expiration.
The API server's decision whether an authenticated identity may perform a verb on a resource. An authenticated request can still be forbidden.
A field that controls whether a ServiceAccount token is mounted into a Pod. Setting it to false removes an API credential the application does not need.

k8s-019.definition: An API object for sensitive values such as passwords or keys. Anyone allowed to read it through the API sees the value, so access must be narrow.
The reversible text encoding used for Secret data. It is not encryption and gives no confidentiality.
Encrypting stored API data in the control plane's storage. It protects against reading that storage directly, not against an authorized API read.
A Secret key mounted as a file in a container. The kubelet can refresh the file later, while an environment variable keeps its starting value.
The application's step of rereading a rotated credential. Without it, the process keeps using the old value until it restarts.

k8s-020.definition: Translating a Service name into an address through cluster DNS. An NXDOMAIN answer fails before any connection is attempted.
The Pod's resolver settings that expand a short name such as hello within the Pod's own namespace, so the same short name elsewhere can mean a different object.
The link from the Service port that clients call to the targetPort on the container. A wrong mapping resolves but reaches no listener.
The server's numeric answer to a request. A 404 proves that some HTTP server answered, so name resolution and the connection already worked.
Testing name resolution, connection, routing and HTTP response in order, so each result narrows where the request failed.

k8s-021.definition: A namespaced object that allows selected traffic to and from Pods. It has an effect only when the network plugin enforces it.
The network implementation that wires Pod networking. Whether it enforces NetworkPolicy decides whether a policy object changes any traffic.
A policy that selects every Pod in a namespace with no ingress rules, so only traffic allowed by another policy can reach them.
NetworkPolicies combine as a union of allows. No policy can subtract traffic that another policy allows.
The policy field choosing which Pods a policy applies to or which peer Pods a rule allows. An empty podSelector selects every Pod in the namespace.

k8s-022.definition: A namespaced request for storage of a given size and access mode, which a Pod mounts by claim name.
A cluster-scoped storage resource that a claim binds to, either created in advance or provisioned dynamically.
An object naming a provisioner and its parameters, used to create PersistentVolumes dynamically for claims that request it.
A workload controller that gives each replica a stable name and its own claim from a volume claim template.
The PersistentVolume setting, Delete or Retain, that decides what happens to the underlying storage after its claim is deleted.

k8s-023.definition: An API object with host and path rules that an Ingress controller uses to route external HTTP traffic to Services.
A family of role-oriented routing APIs, including GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute, that expresses more than Ingress can.
An object that requests listeners, such as a port and protocol, from the implementation named by its GatewayClass.
A Gateway API object that attaches to a Gateway and matches HTTP requests by host, path or header to backend Services.
Checking the presented certificate against a trusted CA and the requested hostname. A TCP connection or HTTP response alone does not establish the TLS contract.

k8s-024.definition: A template-free tool built into kubectl that composes a base of manifests with patches.
A Kustomize directory that reuses a base and applies environment-specific patches, such as a different replica count.
An apply mode in which the API server merges the submitted fields and records which manager owns each one.
The name recorded for the client that set a field under server-side apply.
An error raised when a manager tries to change a field owned by another manager. It is resolved by deciding which manager should own the field.

k8s-025.definition: A package of templates, default values and metadata that Helm renders into Kubernetes manifests.
The values.schema.json file in a chart that constrains the accepted input shape before templates render.
Combining chart templates with values to produce manifests. Reviewing the rendered output shows exactly what would be applied.
A chart resource annotated to run at a release lifecycle point, such as before install or after upgrade.
One installed instance of a chart in a namespace, with its own release metadata and revision history.

k8s-026.definition: A workload controller that runs one copy of a Pod on each eligible node, such as a log or network agent.
A Pod field listing node labels that a node must carry for the Pod to be scheduled there.
Scheduling rules that require or prefer nodes by label expressions, more expressive than nodeSelector.
A node property that repels Pods that do not tolerate it, for example to reserve a node for special workloads.
A Pod field that allows, but does not require, scheduling onto a node with a matching taint.

k8s-027.definition: A measured ratio of user-relevant behavior, such as successful eligible requests divided by all eligible requests.
A target for a service-level indicator over a defined window, such as 99 percent success over one hour.
A numeric measurement collected over time, such as a request counter or a latency histogram.
A quantile found by sorting the values and choosing the one-based position ceil(qn). The convention must be stated with the result.
A request that the indicator's definition counts, so including or excluding a class of requests changes the result.

k8s-028.definition: The lesson's file-based synthetic datastore on a claim, used to prove that data survives a rollout or recovery.
The capstone's collection of independent observations, including a failed-change recovery, that together show the system meets its requirements.
Deliberately shipping one bounded bad change, such as a wrong readiness path, and recovering from it under observation.
Rewriting data from scratch after a failure. It hides data loss, so it cannot count as recovery.
A StatefulSet field that creates one PersistentVolumeClaim per replica, which is kept when the Pod is replaced.

k8s-029.definition: A cluster-scoped registration that adds a new resource type to the API, with its group, names, versions and schema.
One instance of a type defined by a CustomResourceDefinition, stored and served by the API server like built-in objects.
An openAPIV3Schema that declares a type for every field, which the API server uses to validate and prune custom resources.
Whether a resource type is Namespaced or Cluster, which decides where its instances live.
The API server dropping fields that the structural schema does not declare, unless the schema says to preserve them.

k8s-030.definition: A controller with application knowledge that manages that application through custom resources.
The controller cycle that reads current state, compares it with the custom resource's desired state and takes the next corrective action.
The property that repeating an operation does not accumulate unwanted effects, such as setting replicas to 2 instead of incrementing them.
A deletion handshake. A controller removes only its own finalizer after its cleanup is complete, and the object is deleted when none remain.
A typed status entry, read together with observedGeneration, that reports what the controller has achieved for the current spec.

k8s-031.definition: API server checks that run after authentication and authorization and can reject a request before it is persisted.
A built-in policy object that evaluates CEL expressions against a request to allow or deny it, without a webhook.
The separate object that connects a policy to the resources it governs, for example through a namespaceSelector, and sets the action such as Deny.
Common Expression Language, a constrained, side-effect-free expression language used to write admission rules.
A deliberately noncompliant request sent to prove that the policy rejects it for the stated reason.

k8s-032.definition: An object that limits how many selected Pods may be voluntarily disrupted at once, through minAvailable or maxUnavailable.
A deliberate Pod removal, such as a node drain, that respects PodDisruptionBudgets, unlike a node failure.
The API path that removes a Pod only if its PodDisruptionBudget allows it and refuses otherwise.
Cordoning a node and evicting its Pods through the Eviction API before maintenance.
The PodDisruptionBudget status field that reports how many more voluntary disruptions are allowed right now.

k8s-033.definition: A controller that changes a workload's desired replica count from observed metrics and a declared target.
Observed CPU use as a percentage of the Pods' CPU requests, which the autoscaler compares with its target.
The replica number the autoscaler computes from current replicas scaled by the ratio of observed metric to target, before bounds and stabilization apply.
A period over which the autoscaler considers past recommendations, which prevents rapid scale-down flapping.
The aggregated API from which the autoscaler reads resource metrics. When it is unavailable, the autoscaler cannot compute a recommendation.

k8s-034.definition: Sending a small, measured share of traffic to a new version before shifting the rest.
Splitting traffic between versions by explicit weights, which requires a separately qualified traffic implementation rather than replica counts.
A Pod label, such as release=stable, that lets a Service selector choose one version.
A stated condition, measured from application evidence, that must hold before changing traffic.
Editing a Service selector to point at a different set of Pods, which switches traffic quickly and must be reversible.

k8s-035.definition: An opaque string identifying the stored version of an object, used for concurrency checks and for resuming watches.
Updating with the resourceVersion you read, so the server rejects the write if someone changed the object since.
The HTTP status returned when an update carries a stale resourceVersion. The client should reread and reapply its intent.
A long-lived API request that streams changes after a given resourceVersion.
Fetching a fresh full list after a watch reports 410 Gone, because the requested resourceVersion is too old.

k8s-036.definition: The key and value store that holds Kubernetes API state for the control plane.
A point-in-time copy of stored API state. It can restore object specifications but not the bytes inside application volumes.
A separate copy of the data an application stores, such as volume contents, taken with its own consistency method.
The stated limit of what a backup can recover and to which point in time.
A separate environment where a restore is tested without touching the live system.

k8s-037.definition: The supported version differences between control plane components, kubelets and kubectl, which constrain upgrade order.
The announced removal of an API version, so manifests must move to its replacement before an upgrade removes it.
Testing an upgrade by building a new cluster at the target version and moving workloads there, instead of changing the live one.
A table of components and versions known to work together, checked before choosing an upgrade path.
Shifting traffic to the new cluster in a way that can be switched back if checks fail.

k8s-038.definition: A content hash such as sha256 that identifies one exact image, unlike a tag, which can move.
A claim about specific bytes that can be verified under a public key. It does not by itself say why that key should be trusted.
A signed statement about an artifact, such as how it was built or what a scan found.
A record of where and how an artifact was built, including its source and build steps.
A key the verifier has independently decided is authorized to speak for the publisher. A valid signature under any other key proves nothing.

k8s-039.definition: Sharing one cluster among several teams or customers with boundaries between them.
A written analysis of assets, attackers and paths that decides which isolation controls are needed.
A control that separates tenants, such as RBAC, network policy, quotas or separate clusters. A namespace alone does not isolate arbitrary code.
Layering several independent controls so that one failure does not expose a tenant.
A check that a forbidden action fails, such as a cross-tenant request being denied, which shows that a boundary works.

k8s-040.definition: Introducing one known, bounded fault, such as a changed Service selector, to practice detection and repair.
The recorded healthy state before a change, used to tell whether a later observation is abnormal.
The candidate explanation that current evidence best supports, tested next with an observation that distinguishes it from the alternatives.
A Service whose selected endpoint count falls to zero while Pods stay Ready, which points at the selector rather than the application.
An application-level check after a fix that shows the service works again, not just that a status turned green.

k8s-041.definition: The acceptable duration for restoring the defined service after a failure, abbreviated RTO.
The acceptable data-loss window, compared between the last durable data point before failure and the restored one, abbreviated RPO.
An observed recovery duration or data loss, compared with the objective it is meant to meet.
A reviewed, step-by-step recovery procedure with one consistent definition of when recovery starts and finishes.
An intermediate timestamp, such as a Ready Pod, that marks progress but is not the finish until the service and data are verified.

k8s-042.definition: Shipping a versioned platform change, such as a custom resource and its controller, with evidence that each layer works.
The plan prepared before execution, with desired manifests, rendered artifact hashes, image identity, capability receipts and ownership.
A record proving that a host capability, such as a qualified controller, exists before a live gate depends on it.
An object that a controller creates with an owner reference to its parent custom resource.
A blameless written analysis of a bounded incident that covers its timeline, cause, repair and follow-up.

k8s-043.definition: The address assigned to one Pod's network namespace. It is shared by the Pod's containers and changes when the Pod is replaced.
The address of a node's own network interface, distinct from the Pod addresses hosted on that node.
A Service's virtual destination address. It is implemented by forwarding rules that pick an eligible backend, not by one interface.
A Linux kernel view of interfaces, addresses and routes. Each Pod has one, so a test result depends on which namespace the caller used.
Address blocks such as 192.0.2.0/24 reserved for examples, so a sample address is never a real target.

k8s-044.definition: Writing an address block as a prefix and length, such as 10.0.0.0/16, where the length counts the fixed leading bits.
A contiguous address block within a larger range, such as the Pod range assigned to one node.
When several routes match a destination, the one with the most specific matching prefix is chosen.
Two ranges that share addresses, which makes it ambiguous where a packet should go.
The address range from which ClusterIPs are allocated, which must not overlap Pod or node ranges.

k8s-045.definition: All containers in a Pod share one network namespace, so they share an IP address and one port space.
127.0.0.1 or ::1, which reaches only processes in the same network namespace, such as another container in the same Pod.
A helper container, such as a proxy, that runs in the same Pod as the application and shares its network namespace.
Two containers in one Pod trying to bind the same address and port, so the second bind fails.
A process listening on an address other than loopback, often 0.0.0.0 for IPv4, so traffic from outside the Pod can reach it.

k8s-046.definition: The plugin specification the container runtime calls to attach a Pod's network namespace to the network and assign its address.
A virtual network that carries Pod traffic between nodes inside outer packets addressed from node to node.
Wrapping a Pod packet inside an outer packet with node addresses, which adds header bytes to every packet.
The largest packet a link carries without fragmentation. Encapsulation reduces the space left for the inner packet.
How a sender learns the smallest MTU on a path. If its error messages are blocked, large packets fail while small ones still work.

k8s-047.definition: The label query that decides which Pods a Service sends traffic to.
The port that clients connect to on the Service address.
The Pod port that receives forwarded Service traffic. It can be a named port, so backends may use different numbers.
Forwarding by IP address and TCP or UDP port only, without reading HTTP content.
A connection that stays open across many requests. Service balancing happens when it opens, so a new Pod may receive little traffic.

k8s-048.definition: A complete name such as api.study.svc.cluster.local that includes the namespace and cluster domain, so no search expansion is needed.
A suffix from the Pod's resolver settings that is appended to a short name, such as the Pod's own namespace domain.
The configurable DNS suffix for the cluster, typically cluster.local, under which Service names are published.
Stored answers kept until their TTL expires, so a client can keep using an old address after a record changes.
A Service with clusterIP None whose DNS name returns the individual Pod addresses instead of one virtual IP.

k8s-049.definition: An API object listing a subset of a Service's backend addresses, ports and conditions, which forwarding components read.
Marks an endpoint that should receive new traffic, normally matching the Pod's readiness.
Reports whether a backend is still able to serve, even while terminating, so an implementation can fall back to it.
Marks an endpoint whose Pod is shutting down.
A reference from an endpoint to the Pod that backs it, used to trace an address to an object.

k8s-050.definition: The node component that programs Service forwarding rules from Services and EndpointSlices.
A kube-proxy mode that writes Service forwarding rules as Linux iptables chains.
A kube-proxy mode that programs Service forwarding rules through the Linux nftables framework.
A forwarding implementation, often part of the network plugin, that handles Services with kernel eBPF programs instead of kube-proxy rules.
Destination network address translation, which rewrites a packet's destination from the Service address to a chosen backend.

k8s-051.definition: A Service type that opens the same port on every node and forwards it to the Service's backends.
The range from which node ports are allocated, 30000 through 32767 by default.
The node IP a client must reach to use a NodePort, which may be private and unreachable from outside.
Whether a client outside the cluster can actually route to a node address and port through every firewall on the path.

k8s-052.definition: A Service type that asks a cloud integration for an external load balancer in front of the Service.
The component that talks to the provider to create load balancers and writes their address to status.loadBalancer.
The provider's probe of nodes or backends that decides where external traffic is sent.
A LoadBalancer Service with no address in status.loadBalancer yet, often because no controller can provision one.

k8s-053.definition: The proxy implementation that watches Ingress objects and actually routes traffic. Without one, Ingress rules do nothing.
An Ingress rule that matches requests by HTTP host name.
The Ingress field that selects path matching: Exact for one path, or Prefix for matching path elements.
The Ingress field naming which controller should handle the Ingress.

k8s-054.definition: A cluster-scoped object naming the controller that implements Gateways of that class.
A Gateway entry for one port, protocol and optional host name that routes can attach to.
An object in a target namespace that allows routes in another namespace to reference its Services or Secrets.
Per-parent status such as Accepted and ResolvedRefs that reports whether a route attached and whether its backends were found.

k8s-055.definition: The certificate a server presents to prove its name, which the client checks against its trusted roots and the requested host.
The server certificate plus intermediate certificates that link it to a root the client trusts.
Server Name Indication, the TLS field that carries the requested host name so a proxy can choose the right certificate.
The connection from a proxy to its backend, which needs its own TLS and trust settings separate from the client hop.

k8s-056.definition: Source network address translation, which changes a packet's apparent sender, so a backend may see a node address instead of the client.
Kernel state that remembers each translated flow, so replies are translated back correctly.
A Service setting that sends external traffic only to backends on the receiving node, which can preserve the client source address because no second node hop applies SNAT.
An HTTP header that a proxy adds to carry the original client address. It is trustworthy only when a trusted proxy sets it.

k8s-057.definition: DNS records for a headless Service that return Pod addresses and, with a StatefulSet, per-Pod names.
A StatefulSet Pod's name and DNS record, which persist when the Pod is replaced even though its IP may change.
The headless Service named in a StatefulSet's serviceName field, which publishes its per-Pod DNS records.
A Service field that publishes DNS records for Pods before they are ready, for peers that must find each other during startup.

k8s-058.definition: A NetworkPolicy peer field that selects source or destination namespaces by their labels.
How selectors combine: a namespaceSelector and podSelector in the same peer must both match, while separate peers mean either may match.
A Pod becomes isolated in a direction once any policy selects it for that direction, after which only allowed traffic passes.
Policies that select the same Pod combine their allows, so one policy cannot deny what another permits.

k8s-059.definition: A NetworkPolicy rule set that limits outbound connections from the selected Pods.
Pods still need to reach cluster DNS over UDP and TCP, so a strict egress policy must allow it explicitly.
A NetworkPolicy peer that allows an address range in CIDR form, typically for destinations outside the cluster.
Permitting egress by DNS name. The standard NetworkPolicy API cannot express it, although some implementations add it.

k8s-060.definition: Running IPv4 and IPv6 together, so Pods and Services can have an address in each family.
The Service field choosing SingleStack, PreferDualStack or RequireDualStack.
The Service field listing address families. Its first entry is the primary family.
A DNS record that maps a name to an IPv6 address, as an A record does for IPv4.
An IPv6 address written in square brackets, such as `[2001:db8::10]:8080`, so its colons are not read as a port separator.

k8s-061.definition: A well-known node label, such as topology.kubernetes.io/zone, that names the failure domain a node belongs to.
A Service field that expresses a routing preference such as PreferSameZone or PreferSameNode. PreferClose is a deprecated alias.
Preferring backends near the client to reduce latency and cross-zone cost, with fallback when no nearby backend is ready.
A set of infrastructure, such as a zone, that can fail together, so replicas should be spread across several.

k8s-062.definition: Many restarts at once, often from a too strict probe or a shared dependency failure, which adds load and slows recovery.
A shutdown in which a Pod stops receiving new traffic, finishes in-flight work and exits before it is forcibly killed.
Letting existing connections finish while no new ones arrive, so in-flight requests are not cut off.
The time between the termination signal and forced termination. Shutdown work must fit inside it.

k8s-063.definition: A timestamped record of one discrete event from a process.
The record of one request as it crosses services, made of linked spans.
One timed operation within a trace, with a link to its parent and descriptive attributes.
The identifier shared by every span of one request, which lets logs and spans be joined.
A metric label with many distinct values, such as a request ID, that multiplies time series and cost.

k8s-064.definition: An ordered set of checks for name resolution, route reachability, transport connection, TLS identity, proxy routing and application semantics.
Changing one variable between two otherwise identical requests, so a difference in outcome points to that variable.
The first rung of the request ladder where actual behavior differs from the model, which is where diagnosis should focus.
A successful test proves only its own layer, so it cannot be promoted into a claim about every later layer.

k8s-065.definition: An infrastructure layer, often sidecar proxies, that adds traffic management, identity or observability around service communication.
TLS in which both ends present certificates and authenticate each other under an identity system.
A cryptographic identity for a workload that policies can authorize, separate from its changing IP address.
Running services across several clusters, which adds discovery, routing, identity and failure-domain boundaries such as different trust roots.
Retries at several layers multiplying load during a failure, which can turn a partial outage into a full one.

k8s-066.definition: The capstone's written design, with a diagram, manifests, ownership ledger, checks and limitations that align.
A reviewed list of every object to create, its owner and how it is cleaned up.
A table of checks across source validation, admission, controller conditions, endpoints, requests, policy flows, rollout and cleanup.
Exactly one field changed in a copied source, used to show that the checks detect it and that recovery works.
Deleting only the resources recorded as owned by the exercise, so shared objects survive.
